titulo: Present subjunctive (forms): The swapped vowel: regular forms

aula.objetivo: Form the present subjunctive of regular verbs, of irregular verbs from the «yo» form («tenga», «haga», «diga»), of stem-changing verbs and of the six verbs with their own forms («sea», «esté», «vaya», «haya», «sepa», «dé»), with the spelling changes (busque, llegue, empiece).

blocos.titulo: The subjunctive recipe: drop the «-o» and swap the vowel
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the subjunctive is a set of verb forms that Spanish uses after certain expressions, like «quiero que» or «es importante que». English has it too, but only as relics: "I suggest that he BE on time", "It's important that she GO", "God save the King", "Long live the Queen", "If I WERE you". In each case English uses an odd form ("be", "go", "save", "were") instead of the expected "is", "goes", "saves", "was". Spanish kept a full set of these forms and uses them every day, in ordinary conversation — not as something formal or old-fashioned. In this lesson you only learn to FORM them; the uses come in lessons 43 and 44. STEP 2: first, take the «yo» form of the present: «hablo», «como», «vivo». STEP 3: drop the final «-o»: «habl-», «com-», «viv-». STEP 4: add the SWAPPED vowel. -ar verbs switch to «e»: hable, hables, hable, hablemos, habléis, hablen. -er and -ir verbs switch to «a»: coma, comas, coma, comamos, comáis, coman; viva, vivas, viva, vivamos, viváis, vivan. STEP 5: to remember it: -ar verbs are the "a" verbs, so in the subjunctive they flip to «e»; -er and -ir verbs are the "e/i" verbs, so they flip to «a». STEP 6: the «yo» form is the same as the «él, ella, usted» form: «que yo hable» and «que él hable». When it could be confusing, use the pronoun. STEP 7: only the «vosotros» form has an accent: «habléis, comáis, viváis». In Latin America, «ustedes» is used instead: «hablen, coman, vivan». STEP 8: you've already used these forms in commands: the usted imperative and the negative tú imperative ARE subjunctive: «Hable más despacio», «No hables tan rápido», «Coma algo».
blocos.comparacao: English has a subjunctive too, but only as fossils: "I suggest that he BE here", "It's essential that she ATTEND", "If I WERE you". Spanish uses its subjunctive all the time, in everyday speech. The good news: you already know some forms from the commands «Hable más despacio» and «No hables tan rápido» — that's the subjunctive.

erros.motivo: In -ar verbs, the «tú» ending in the subjunctive is «-es».
In -ar verbs, swap «a» for «e» in «vosotros» too.
English "I want YOU TO COME" can't be copied: when the subject changes, Spanish uses «que» + subjunctive.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud the six subjunctive forms of «cantar» and «beber» («cante, cantes, cante…», «beba, bebas, beba…»). Then say: «Hable más despacio, por favor» and «No hables tan rápido».
Say out loud the «yo» form of the present of hablar, comer, vivir, tener, hacer, decir and salir («hablo, como, vivo, tengo…»). These forms are the basis of this lesson.
